newsitem.title: FRANCE: Western carmakers study Korean production - Calvet.
newsitem.headline: Western carmakers study Korean production - Calvet.

text.p: European carmakers concerned about the rapid inroads of South Korean carmakers into the European market should focus on subsidies and currency rates, said chairman Jacques Calvet, the outgoing chairman of the European carmakers' association ACEA.
Calvet, who also is PSA Peugeot Citroen chairman, said the association had set up a working group to study Korean carmakers' operations in Europe.
"I think we need to look at the level of the won," he told reporters, adding that he believed the Korean currency was undervalued by 50 percent against European currencies.
He said dumping did not appear to be a factor, as the Korean carmakers were selling cars at higher prices in Europe than in their home market, but he said subsidies should be examined.

He said subsidies for Korean car production in eastern European countries seeking to enter the European Union such as Poland and Romania should be studied to see "if they correspond to European subsidy regulations".
Calvet said U.S. and Korean carmakers were also trying to determine the source of funding for car businesses in Korea that are often branches of bigger conglomerates.

Their concern has been raised by the Koreans' ambitious production objectives and by the rapid growth of their share of the European market, to 1.8 percent this year from less than 0.2 percent in 1990.
Over the same period, the Europeans' share of the Korean market has more slowly, to 0.4 percent from 0.1 percent, according to ACEA.
Calvet was elected chairman of the ACEA last January for a one-year term.
